headline: High-risk filesystem and code-execution overlap: Open Interpreter can alter local files while pdf.js processes PDFs, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read/write the filesystem and use clipboard/stdin, while pdf.js reads PDF files. If Open Interpreter ingests PDF-derived text or copied content from pdf.js, malicious PDF content could steer instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, but the bridge is indirect rather than a shared MCP channel.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is pointed at text copied from pdf.js-rendered PDFs
IF pdf.js output is manually pasted into Open Interpreter without provenance labels
mitigations: Disable copy/paste between the tools during review sessions
Use separate workspaces for PDF review and agent execution
Add a manual provenance note before any pasted content
Review PDFs in a read-only viewer before handing text to Open Interpreter

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and can write the filesystem; pdf.js handles PDF documents. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose PDF contents or adjacent local files through outputs or logs. The blast radius includes sensitive documents, but both agents are local and no third-party upload is indicated for pdf.js.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF PDF files contain sensitive data and Open Interpreter reads or summarizes them
mitigations: Move PDFs into a dedicated review folder
Restrict Open Interpreter to a narrow working directory
Clear terminal scrollback after handling sensitive PDFs
Avoid opening confidential PDFs in the same session as file-writing automation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. pdf.js also reads PDF files in the workspace. If both touch the same directory, concurrent edits or generated artifacts can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. This is dangerous by default because Open Interpreter can mutate shared files without coordination.
conditions: IF both agents write into the same repository or working directory
IF Open Interpreter runs with auto_run or unattended file edits
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Pause Open Interpreter before pdf.js batch processing
Commit or stash git changes before running either tool
Use filesystem locks or a simple manual handoff checklist

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate or modify files based on local content, and pdf.js processes PDFs that may be treated as source material. If Open Interpreter's output is fed into pdf.js workflows or vice versa without verification, errors can propagate into downstream documents or actions. pdf.js is not an action-taking agent, so this is a workflow-quality risk rather than an irreversible one.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter-generated text is reused as authoritative input to PDF processing
IF a human does not verify extracted text before downstream use
mitigations: Require a human review step before reuse of extracted text
Mark generated files as draft until checked
Compare key fields against the source PDF manually
Keep pdf.js outputs separate from action-bearing automation

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter can touch local files and model-provider API keys, while pdf.js is a local PDF processor with no secrets or network egress. The main compliance issue is local handling of sensitive PDFs in a general-purpose automation environment, not a documented residency or certification mismatch. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because no cross-jurisdiction flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs are processed in the same local workspace as Open Interpreter
IF organizational policy forbids general-purpose automation on sensitive documents
mitigations: Use non-sensitive sample PDFs for automation tests
Store regulated PDFs in a separate access-controlled folder
Disable API-key exposure in the Open Interpreter session
Document the local-only handling path for compliance review
